svg.title: The daemon
svg.desc: Tabs follow the same rule, one by one, so that the tabs agents leave behind don't pile up in a daemon that other agents keep busy. A tab no command has used for a third of the limit (5 minutes) rests: Umbra hides its window, and the page slows its timers and pauses its animations as a background tab does in Safari. The next command on it shows it again and runs once the page knows it is visible. A tab unused for the whole limit closes, and its web process ends with it; a later command that names it says so, and open --tab NAME <url> opens it again. A tab never rests while active or queued work targets it, a handoff shows it, a download is active, a lease protects it, or trusted form input marked it dirty, and a tab that closes while it was the current one leaves no current tab, so a command without --tab never lands in another agent's tab. On the way out it saves the session cookies of keepSession and keepSignedIn sites (see sites.md).
